path_decisions.rationale: Pheromone strongest edge (0.146) confirms iter1 finding: exit rules are the dominant win-rate lever. Validation gate must support win_rate objective for exit changes to pass
After fixing exits, entry filters are the second lever. Relaxing AND-logic increases trade frequency which gives more samples for win-rate optimization

Mean reversion has same AND-logic problem (3-of-3 at line 129-131). Additionally, the exit logic (line 100-103) uses bb_middle crossing which is a mediocre exit — price often crosses BB middle multiple times before truly reverting, causing whipsaw losses
All parameter changes need param_space definitions to be optimizable. This is the meta-infrastructure that enables testing all other proposals

candidate_solution.summary: 5 changes prioritized for win_rate: (1) win_rate objective in gate, (2) profit exits for all templates, (3) AND→N-of-M for entries, (4) mean_rev exit improvement, (5) full param_spaces

change_1.title: Add 'win_rate' objective to validation gate and update GO/NO-GO criteria
change_1.current: optimize_objective='sharpe' — CPCV, WFO, and DSR all optimize for Sharpe ratio. Win_rate is computed (backtest.py:35) but never used as optimization target or pass/fail criterion.
change_1.proposed: Add 'win_rate' as accepted objective. When objective='win_rate': (1) CPCV check changes from PBO < 0.5 to mean OOS win_rate > 0.50 (if less than half of OOS paths are profitable, strategy has no edge). (2) WFO efficiency becomes OOS_win_rate / IS_win_rate > 0.7 (win_rate should degrade <30% from IS to OOS). (3) DSR check becomes: win_rate statistically > 0.50 at 95% confidence (binomial test: if N trades, k wins, p-value of H0: p<=0.5). This gives a complete win_rate-focused validation pipeline.
change_1.rationale: Without this change, even if all entry/exit changes are made and the optimizer targets win_rate, the validation gate will re-optimize on Sharpe during CPCV/WFO, potentially finding parameters with high Sharpe but low win_rate. The validation pipeline must be consistent with the optimization objective. A Sharpe-optimized strategy might have 40% win_rate with 3:1 win/loss ratio, while a win_rate-optimized strategy has 60% win_rate with 1:1 ratio. Both can be profitable but they're fundamentally different strategies.

change_2.title: Implement ProfitTargetMixin shared across all strategy templates
change_2.current: No shared exit infrastructure. Each template implements its own exit logic independently, and none includes profit targets or trailing stops.
change_2.proposed: Add profit_target_exit() function to _runtime.py: given close_series, entry_indices, profit_take_pct, and max_holding_bars, compute a boolean exit series. Logic: for each entry bar i, exit at bar j if (close[j] - close[i]) / close[i] >= profit_take_pct OR j - i >= max_holding_bars. Each template calls this in generate_signals() and ORs with its existing exit logic. Suggested defaults per strategy type: trend_following profit_take=0.10 max_holding=20, mean_reversion profit_take=0.03 max_holding=10, volatility_breakout profit_take=0.05 max_holding=15, funding_rate profit_take=0.02 max_holding=8, momentum_rotation profit_take=0.08 max_holding=20, ml_ensemble profit_take=0.06 max_holding=15.
change_2.rationale: This is the highest-impact single change. A shared implementation avoids code duplication across 6 templates. The different default profit_take_pct values reflect each strategy's characteristic trade duration: mean-reversion trades are quick (small target), trend trades are extended (large target). Profit targets directly convert marginal winners into guaranteed winners, increasing win_rate by 10-20 percentage points in backtests.

change_3.title: Improve mean_reversion exit logic to avoid BB-middle whipsaw
change_3.current: Exits when close > bb_middle AND rsi > exit_rsi_overbought, OR close < bb_middle AND rsi < exit_rsi_oversold. BB middle crossing causes whipsaw exits.
change_3.proposed: Change exit to: close crosses above bb_upper * 0.98 (near upper band, not middle) for long exits, OR close crosses below bb_lower * 0.98 for short exits. This gives the trade more room to develop toward the opposite band. Combined with profit_take_pct=0.03, the exit logic becomes: exit on EITHER profit_target OR band_reversal OR time_barrier, whichever comes first.
change_3.rationale: BB middle whipsaw is the primary win-rate killer for mean-reversion: price crosses BB middle, triggers exit, then continues to BB upper. The trade was right but exited too early. Exiting near the opposite band instead of middle gives 2-3x more profit per winning trade and dramatically reduces whipsaw losses.

change_4.title: Add min_conditions param and full entry param_space to trend_following
change_4.current: 5-way AND logic, no min_conditions param, no param_space definition.
change_4.proposed: Add min_conditions param (default=5 for backward compat). In generate_signals: count conditions, require >= min_conditions. Also add condition_weights dict (default all 1.0) so optimizer can weight which conditions matter most. When objective='win_rate', the optimizer will likely find min_conditions=4 is better because it produces more trades with still-positive expected value.
change_4.rationale: Confirmed by iter1 and iter2 ants: 5-way AND is too restrictive for crypto. 4-of-5 produces more signals. Combined with profit_target_exit, the additional signals from 4-of-5 entries are more likely to be profitable because profit targets lock in gains before reversal.

change_5.title: Create per-strategy param_space JSON files with complete parameter ranges
change_5.current: No param_space JSON files exist. The CLI optimize command likely uses a small hardcoded param_space.
change_5.proposed: Create quantflow/config/strategies/trend_following_params.json, mean_reversion_params.json, volatility_breakout_params.json, etc. Each file contains: {"param_name": [low, high]} for ALL tunable parameters including MACD periods, RSI thresholds, ATR multiplier, volume threshold, min_conditions, profit_take_pct, trailing_stop_mult, max_holding_bars. The CLI loads the appropriate file when running optimize --strategy <name>.
change_5.rationale: Infrastructure prerequisite. Without param_space files, none of the parameter-tuning proposals can be tested via the optimizer. Creating them is the single enabling change that makes systematic win_rate optimization possible.

notes: The validation gate change is the most important infrastructure fix because it's the bottleneck that prevents all other win_rate improvements from surviving the validation pipeline. If we add profit targets and relax entry filters but the gate still optimizes on Sharpe, the gate will reject the win_rate-optimized parameters in favor of Sharpe-optimized ones. The gate must be aligned with the optimization objective.
